acceptanceCriteria: The owner records an explicit decision that accepts, amends or rejects each proposed addition, with the closed main-framework set per supported language.
Each accepted addition is attached to V1-0632 or a language parent (V1-0592, V1-0593, V1-0594) or filed as its own ticket; no duplicate umbrella is created.
Unaccepted or deferred frameworks are recorded as explicit exclusions rather than implied coverage.
body:
Question for the owner: which frameworks form the closed main-framework set for CEM 1.0 runner coverage (V1-0591)?

A scratch audit at source commit a5326ba6 (main-framework-gap-audit/1, status PROPOSED_MAIN_SET_WITH_CONFIRMED_INVENTORY_GAPS_NOT_RELEASE_QUALIFICATION) found 61 listed execution IDs and 55 concrete experimental profiles, none stable-qualified, and proposes these additions that have no dedicated profile or ticket today:
- Go: Ginkgo v2 spec-level profile (plan approved with conditions on 2026-10-01; runtime NOT_RUN)
- Python: doctest qualification, behave scenarios
- JavaScript/TypeScript: Jasmine, Cucumber-JS
- Ruby: Cucumber-Ruby
- Java/Kotlin/Android: Cucumber-JVM (Java and Kotlin tuples), Compose UI assertion qualification
- Swift/Objective-C: Quick
- C/JNI: CMocka (integration in progress), Unity, JNI behavioural bridge
- C++: doctest, Boost.Test
- HTML/CSS, shader (GLSL/Metal), structured data (JSON/YAML/TOML): named application assertion tuples

The audit acquired and ran no framework software, was not independently reviewed, and used a literal queue search (no hits for Ginkgo, Jasmine, Cucumber, doctest, Boost, Robot, nose2, tSQLt, shader, JNI at head sequence 1804), which is not proof of global absence. This is a scope question, not a confirmed defect. Popularity was not ranked and completeness is not claimed.
title: Decide the closed main-framework set for CEM 1.0 runner coverage
